_comment: Shipped defaults. Resolution order, later wins, shallow-merged per top-level key: (1) this file, (2) ~/.config/claude-qa-manager/config.json (user-level: credentials, policy), (3) <repo>/.claude/skills/qa-cycle/config.json (project-level: targets, schema files). A project should never need to restate credentials, and a user config should never need to know a repo's layout.

targets._comment: Optional. Branches are derived at runtime from the MR/PR itself, so single-repo projects need NO targets at all. Declare targets only for a monorepo whose submodules are reviewed independently. See examples/monorepo-submodules.json.

schema._comment: Paths that ARE the database schema -- the file(s) a provisioner reads to create a new tenant/instance. Empty by default: when empty the schema gate reports 'skipped:not-configured' and NEVER silently passes. Match on path only; do NOT add DDL content scanning (see docs/CASE-STUDIES.md #schema-drift).

contract._comment: How a ticket id is recognised in an MR/PR title or body.

qa_agent._comment: Optional separate identity for QA-attributed actions (round notes, approvals). Fix commits and pushes always use the developer's own credentials. When unresolvable, the plugin degrades gracefully: notes post under the dev identity and approval is skipped entirely.

progress._comment: How long the lens fan-out may go quiet before a renderer calls it stalled. The status file is rewritten when a lens RETURNS, so the legitimate silence between writes is however long your slowest lens takes -- which is a property of YOUR repo and diff, not of this tool. A 595-line diff on a large monorepo ran 8-20 minutes per lens; a small service may finish in seconds, and there a 20-minute fuse means a genuinely wedged round goes unnoticed for 20 minutes. Tune it down for a fast project, up for a slow one. Only the fan-out needs this: the manager's own merge/render/post phases are bounded work and use a short fixed threshold. QA_STATUS_LENS_STALL_SECONDS overrides it without touching config.

verify._comment: How a fix is verified before it is committed. Normally EMPTY: the target's own test/build entry point is DISCOVERED from its Makefile, package.json, tox.ini, go.mod, etc. Any decent project already declares how it is tested, and restating that here duplicates it -- the copy then drifts and the gate certifies a command the project stopped using. Set `command` only when detection is wrong. When nothing is discoverable the gate reports state 'none-found' and the round note must say the fixes went unverified; it NEVER reports a pass.

review._comment: Panel width is capped at 6 -- the measured concurrency ceiling for agent grandchildren, which keeps the panel a single wave. Narrow a target's lens_tags rather than overriding the panel by hand, and never manage cost by downgrading the model: a cheaper reviewer is a weaker reviewer, which defeats the cycle.

sast_gate._comment: Behaviour when a security pipeline is still running on an approval-eligible round. Poll cadence is deliberately coarse to stay friendly to prompt caching.
